title: Marx's value-form across editions: Form IV and editors in Marx's name
description: These historical theses read Capital's value-form derivation across its editions: the first-edition appendix performs Forms I to IV explicitly, while the 1872 text keeps the polar rule for a single expression and drops the only form in which the system-level consequence was written. They hold that Form IV voids the socially valid display of magnitude and resolves into the fetish, and that the theory of the medium stands at an editorial cut in Capital as it stands at the lost notebook of the 1844 manuscripts. Backhaus's pre-monetary misreading, Engels's interventions, the 1932 Landshut–Mayer edition and the philological quarantine of early manuscripts are read as editing in Marx's name.

claims.statement: The appendix performs the derivation in four numbered forms — I through IV — with an explicitness that the later editions smooth over. In the appendix, Marx shows his work. The reader can see each step of the progressive graph simplification. The transitions are labored, difficult, sometimes repetitive — and the difficulty IS the content. The value-form derivation is not "hard to understand" because Marx was a bad writer. It is hard because the operation it describes is hard: the emergence of a universal equivalent from a structure that does not logically require one.

claims.statement: The German is sharper: *Die Philosophen haben die Welt nur verschieden interpretiert; es kömmt drauf an, sie zu verändern.* The *nur* ("only") is doing the work — it converts all prior philosophy into a preparation for this sentence. The *es kömmt drauf an* is not "the point is" but something closer to "what it comes down to" — a colloquial urgency, a street-corner exhortation written in a notebook Marx never published, in a set of theses he scrawled in Brussels in the spring of 1845 and then set aside. The notebook was found after Marx's death.

claims.registered_title: Monetary Dark Matter: Constitutive Labor, Obligating Provenance, and the Shear into Money-Form
claims.statement: Form IV operates one level up: it runs every expression simultaneously and reads the resulting system reflexively. No individual equation breaks the polar rule. The system does something the polar rule does not govern, and what it does is void the socially valid display of magnitude.
claims.falsifier: It fails if the reflexive structure can be shown to be already implied by Forms I–III, such that Form IV adds no writable state.

claims.registered_title: Monetary Dark Matter: Constitutive Labor, Obligating Provenance, and the Shear into Money-Form
claims.statement: What 1872 keeps is the prohibition that governs a single expression of value; what it drops is the only form in which the system-level consequence was written. In §1 of the 1872 text Marx raises the back-reference explicitly — *20 Ellen Leinwand = 1 Rock* also implies *1 Rock = 20 Ellen Leinwand* — and immediately disciplines it: invert the equation and linen becomes the equivalent instead of the coat, so the same commodity cannot occupy both positions. The reflexive move is acknowledged at the level where it is harmless and foreclosed there. The level at which it is not harmless has no form left to write it in.

claims.registered_title: Monetary Dark Matter: Constitutive Labor, Obligating Provenance, and the Shear into Money-Form
claims.statement: In the Paris manuscripts of 1844, the claims about the medium of meaning — language given to every thinker as a social product, the element of thought itself as sensuous in nature, general consciousness capable of becoming an abstraction from real life that confronts it with hostility — stand at the edge of the physical hole where the second notebook was lost, and Marx never developed them. In *Capital*, the form that would describe a monetary body carrying meaning stands at an editorial cut. Different mechanisms, same location. **The theory of the medium is at the cut in both cases.**
